goal: Reuse the official provider SDK and enable fixed project dependency preparation without broadening the competition architecture.
changes: Replace the production hand-written Chat HTTP call with official openai 2.30.0 Chat Completions; retain durable budget, bounded I/O, canonical request identity and unknown-result protection.
Provide OpenAI/DeepSeek defaults and compatible base URL/model/key-environment configuration; optional output-token parameter and provider mode remain explicit.
Accept standard nullable SDK response fields and preserve refusal/incomplete/unknown usage; historical cloud-httpx profiles remain read-only.

ApplicationProfile read-only preflight declares full project/tool/device/signing/oracle prerequisites; optional preparation executes in independent baseline and candidate copies and retains source bindings/receipts.
Keep npm caches in the owned execution project; ohpm/Hvigor cache arguments and real replay runners remain pending.
Bound Windows same-path atomic rename retry to 5/32 errors, 5 attempts and 250ms waiting; persistent denial preserves rollback and never repeats an edit/model/external action.

validation.scope: Official SDK MockTransport, declared-prerequisite preflight and short synthetic executables. No cloud or HarmonyOS execution.

totals.basis: Latest observed result per these five groups, not a full-repository or effect evaluation.

first_failures.reason: Cold SDK lazy import exhausted the ordinary fixture's 2-second allowance; fixture uses 10 seconds now, deterministic deadline test and production limits unchanged.
44 passed, 2 random Windows rename denials, 1 symlink skip.
Same fixture failure class repeated; addressed by bounded same-operation filesystem contention handling.
New rename test assumed LF baseline but fixture used Windows CRLF. Assert exact original bytes instead.

limitations: Real provider compatibility and model identifier are unverified; native Anthropic/Gemini protocols, streaming and arbitrary vendor extensions are outside current scope.
HarmonyOS SDK/signing/device provisioning and actual replay/behavior/regression runners require first-case acceptance; placeholder profile is blocked.
Method effect and competition metrics remain unknown.
